coverage_gaps: The merged universe is still biased toward U.S.-listed companies and U.S. ADRs; later layers should add Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Europe, A-share, and H-share suppliers across HBM, substrates, interposers, OSAT, optical modules, cooling, and power equipment.

HBM supplier coverage is incomplete because SK hynix and Samsung Electronics are not yet fully represented in this JSON universe despite being central HBM suppliers; later validation should add local tickers and primary filings.

Advanced packaging substrate, interposer, ABF substrate, thermal material, and connector suppliers are underrepresented; this is a key Serenity gap because bottlenecks may migrate below the foundry/OSAT layer.
Optical-module and transceiver coverage is narrow; later layers should map U.S., Taiwan, China, and Japan suppliers of 800G/1.6T optics, lasers, DSPs, silicon photonics, and CPO-related components.

Power/cooling coverage is preliminary; later layers should add liquid-cooling specialists, electrical switchgear vendors, transformer suppliers, UPS vendors, grid EPC firms, and utilities with direct data-center exposure.

Cybersecurity coverage is thematic rather than evidence-rich; later validation should test whether procurement rules, SBOM requirements, identity controls, and secure-by-design mandates are creating incremental demand for specific vendors.
Software and cloud candidates are demand aggregators rather than bottleneck owners; later layers should distinguish capex beneficiaries from margin-accretive software monetization.

No current valuation or market-pricing check has been performed in Layer 1C; later layers should compare market-implied expectations against evidence without issuing buy/sell recommendations or target prices.

Evidence strength varies sharply: NVDA, TSM, MU, AMKR, KLAC, ONTO, TER, FORM, ENTG, MSFT, ANET, and AVGO have cached evidence, while many additional breadth candidates are inference-stage and require primary-source validation.

memory_update.text: Technology Layer 1 should be tracked as an AI infrastructure stack, not a single software or semiconductor trade: demand originates in AI/cloud workloads and propagates through accelerators, HBM, foundry, packaging, networking, cybersecurity, and power/cooling/grid constraints.

The highest-priority chokepoint lane remains AI accelerators plus HBM plus advanced-node foundry plus advanced packaging, because the bottleneck can migrate across these capacity and qualification layers.

Process control, inspection, metrology, probe cards, and automated test should stay in the funnel because HBM and advanced packaging complexity can make yield learning and qualification a hidden bottleneck.

AI networking and optical interconnect deserve independent treatment from compute accelerators because cluster utilization, latency, bandwidth, and congestion control can constrain the effective value of installed GPUs.

Data-center power, cooling, and grid infrastructure are first-order technology nodes because AI deployment can be constrained by time-to-power, thermal density, interconnection queues, and firm clean-power availability.

Layer 2 should add non-U.S. public suppliers in Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Europe, China, and Hong Kong, especially HBM, substrates, optical modules, advanced packaging equipment, thermal, and power-equipment suppliers.

Layer 2 should convert inference-stage candidates into evidence-ranked candidates using primary filings, investor presentations, customer/qualification evidence, revenue mix, backlog, capex, and market-pricing checks.

summary: Layer 1C merged the Technology Layer 1 universe into a broad AI-infrastructure-centered research universe spanning accelerators, HBM, foundry, advanced packaging, semiconductor equipment, optical/networking, cloud AI platforms, automation software, cybersecurity, and data-center power/cooling/grid infrastructure. Ranking prioritizes Serenity relevance: proximity to measurable AI demand, control of scarce or qualification-heavy supply-chain nodes, bottleneck plausibility, evidence strength from cached Layer 1A/1B materials, and breadth across the theme. This is a research-prioritization universe only, not a buy/sell list or return forecast.
universe_method: multi-step: theme decomposition -> node expansion -> dedupe/rank
